detailed_rationale:
Devyani International is India's largest Yum Brands franchisee (KFC, Pizza Hut) and also runs Costa Coffee, under the RJ Corp umbrella. The quant sheet shows a business still growing top-line at a healthy clip (revenue_growth_1y 13.3%, 3yr CAGR 23.2%, though the latter flatters off a low COVID-era base) but structurally thin at the bottom line: ROE -1.56% (3yr average -3.47%), ROCE 4.75%, and interest coverage under 3.1x. Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026) sales were Rs 1,581cr (+16.5% YoY) with EBITDA of Rs 255cr (~16% margin) but net profit of only Rs 17cr, and FY26 as a whole closed with a net loss of Rs 43cr on Rs 5,611cr sales. The negative trailing EPS is why pe_current shows as a meaningless -356x in the quant sheet; on P/B the stock trades at 9.24x, which is a rich multiple for a business currently destroying rather than compounding book value.

The defining event for this name is the announced all-stock merger with Sapphire Foods (swap ratio of 177 Devyani shares per Sapphire share, ~$934mn combined deal value), which exchanges have now cleared; management (Ravi Jaipuria) is framing the combined entity as India's largest F&B franchise platform crossing $1bn revenue, consolidating 3,000+ KFC/Pizza Hut stores. This is a genuine structural change the standalone quant history cannot price in - two years of trailing ratios describe a company that is about to be restructured. Debt (~Rs 3,833cr) is elevated relative to equity, but a meaningful share of QSR sector 'debt' is Ind AS 116 lease-liability capitalization for the store network, not conventional balance-sheet leverage - so the raw D/E overstates distress somewhat versus a manufacturing peer, though interest coverage at ~3x still leaves little room for error if margins soften further.

Management's own framing (per recent coverage) is a 'back-to-basics' push, explicitly to revive the underperforming Pizza Hut chain via the Sapphire tie-up and improve store economics rather than just adding units. That is an admission the current store base isn't earning its keep - consistent with the negative ROE - and it will take several quarters of execution to show up in the P&L.
recommendation_rationale: The quant score already lands on Hold on both 1yr and 3yr views, and nothing in the fundamentals argues for a rescue to a stronger stance in either direction. Revenue growth and store expansion are real, but negative ROE, a net loss in the most recent full year, and thin interest coverage rule out anything constructive; conversely, the growth trajectory, EBITDA margin recovery signs, and the strategic logic of the Sapphire consolidation are real enough that a Sell call would be premature ahead of merger completion. Hold is the honest call while the merger plays out.
summary: Devyani (KFC/Pizza Hut/Costa Coffee franchisee) continues to grow revenue at a healthy pace but is not yet consistently profitable - it posted a net loss for FY26 and thin net margins in the latest quarter. The pending all-stock merger with Sapphire Foods will reshape the company into India's largest QSR franchise platform over the next 12-18 months, but that also means today's standalone financial history is a poor guide to what the combined business will look like. We rate it a Hold: real growth, but profitability and merger-integration execution both still need to be proven.
positive_para: Devyani has built genuine scale as Yum Brands' largest India franchisee, with revenue compounding at a low-20s% 3-year CAGR and Q1 FY27 sales still growing 16.5% YoY with EBITDA margin around 16%. The Sapphire Foods merger, once completed, creates a combined platform with 3,000+ stores and a stated ambition to cross $1bn in revenue - giving the combined entity negotiating scale with Yum Brands, shared back-end/supply-chain economics, and a credible plan (management's own words) to fix the chronically underperforming Pizza Hut chain. DII ownership has been rising (to 18.84%) even as FII holding has thinned, suggesting domestic institutional conviction in the long-term consumption/QSR-penetration story.
negative_para: The uncomfortable fact is that Devyani lost money in FY26 (-Rs 43cr) and 3-year average ROE is negative (-3.47%) - this is not a temporarily depressed compounder, it is a business that has not yet proven it can turn store growth into shareholder returns, even as it trades at 9.24x book value. Interest coverage of ~3x leaves little cushion if input costs or discretionary urban consumption soften further (a live risk given broader FY26 commentary on urban demand). The Sapphire merger is the single biggest swing factor for the stock and it cuts both ways: management's own 'back-to-basics' language for Pizza Hut is effectively an admission that a meaningful chunk of the existing store base is underperforming, and merging two still-maturing QSR balance sheets carries real integration risk over the 15-18 month completion window - this is exactly the kind of event where the quant history stops being a reliable guide.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At 9.24x P/B against a currently negative ROE, the market is pricing a recovery story, not today's earnings - it needs OPM to normalize back toward the high-teens levels the QSR majors have shown in better years and same-store-sales to re-accelerate, which is a fair-value-to-rich multiple for a business that lost money last year. This is not a stretched 'hypergrowth' valuation, but it is not cheap on trailing fundamentals either; it is a bet on execution (margin recovery + successful Sapphire integration) that has not yet shown up in the numbers.
escalation_reason: Devyani is mid-merger with Sapphire Foods (also in this batch, ticker SAPPHIRE) - an all-stock combination already cleared by exchanges, swap ratio 177 Devyani shares per Sapphire share, targeted completion 15-18 months out. The standalone quant history and score for both tickers describe companies that are about to be structurally combined; a PM view on either name really needs a combined-entity/merger-arb lens rather than two independent Hold calls, and the eventual accounting treatment/dilution is not something the point-in-time quant data can see.

technical_commentary: Clean, unambiguous downtrend since the 2023 peak (214.4): three consecutive years of lower highs and lower lows have dragged price to -48% off its all-time high, fully below an inverted bearish moving-average stack (40m>20m>10m>price). Volume has picked up on the way down over the last six months (1.4x the prior run-rate), a sign the decline is still being sold into rather than stabilizing, though the one recent volume spike (Feb-26, +9.7%) bears watching for early basing signs.
